papers.title: Improving sleep monitoring in athletes: a comparative evaluation of four automated sleep scoring algorithms on 204 polysomnography recordings.
papers.summary: Evaluated four automated sleep scoring algorithms (Luna, U-Sleep, YASA, GSSC) against manual polysomnography in 204 recordings from 75 athletes, assessing accuracy, robustness, and clinical agreement. GSSC achieved the highest macro F1 (0.76), was most robust to signal degradation, and reliably predicted total sleep time, sleep onset latency, and wake after sleep onset with minimal bias.

papers.title: Sleep fragmentation drives local, network-specific epileptic activity in human epilepsy
papers.summary: Using combined stereo-EEG and polysomnography in patients with epilepsy, this study found that experimentally induced sleep arousals cause rapid, local increases in interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) confined to neocortical regions, with a larger effect in N2 than N3 sleep. Arousals did not alter IED spatial propagation, suggesting state-dependent enhancement of local cortical excitability without broader network recruitment.

papers.title: TopoAdapter: a plug-and-play multi-hop topology adapter for MI-EEG decoding.
papers.summary: Introduced TopoAdapter, a plug-and-play input module that injects a fixed electrode-layout topology prior into existing EEG backbones for motor imagery decoding. It improved mean accuracy on BCI Competition IV-2a (+1.17 percentage points), Zhou2016 (+0.13), and High-Gamma executed-movement (+0.36) datasets, and added only 70 parameters compared to 506 for a competing adaptive layer.

papers.title: Neural Architectures of Slow and Fast Dynamics in the Human Brain
papers.summary: Using SPLIT on large-scale intracranial sEEG (8,619 contacts, 185 individuals), the study identified dissociable fast (~10-100 Hz) and slow (~1-10 Hz) temporal components. Fast timescales followed a sensorimotor-to-association cortical hierarchy, whereas slow timescales showed no hierarchical gradient but covaried with heart rate and were enriched at heart-related neural response sites, persisting across wakefulness, rest, sleep, and anesthesia.

papers.title: Multimodal Respiratory Event Detection Leveraging Signal Complementarity under Intermittent SpO₂ Loss.
papers.summary: The authors evaluated probability-level late fusion of EEG, ECG, SpO2, and abdominal effort classifiers for sleep apnea detection in 148 patients, using placeholder probabilities for unreliable SpO2 epochs. Abdominal effort alone reached macro-F1 0.996 and SpO2 plus abdominal effort reached 0.997, while ECG plus EEG outperformed SpO2-inclusive pairs; performance remained stable despite 30.7% SpO2 dropout, suggesting signal complementarity mattered more than modality count.

papers.title: Sleep renormalizes learning-perturbed cortical dynamics to stabilize memory
papers.summary: High-density EEG in humans after declarative learning and a matched non-learning control showed that learning displaced cortical population dynamics during wakefulness, followed by opposing reorganization during NREM sleep. The sleep response was constrained by the preceding waking perturbation across time, cortical space, and individuals, and predicted sleep-specific memory benefit beyond either state alone.

papers.title: Reciprocal brain-behavior associations in gambling disorder revealed by theta cordance and directional predictive modeling.
papers.summary: This retrospective observational study compared resting-state theta cordance in 28 men with DSM-5 gambling disorder and 29 healthy controls, finding lower central and higher left parietal cordance in patients, with trend-level occipital and left temporal differences. No cordance-clinical correlations were significant, but exploratory VAR-based directional modeling identified asymmetric reciprocal predictive associations between prefrontal/frontocentral cordance and SOGS and between central/right temporal cordance and illness duration.

papers.title: An Interpretable EEG Machine Learning Prototype for Alzheimers Disease Classification
papers.summary: The study developed an interpretable subject-level EEG classifier for Alzheimer's disease versus healthy controls using the OpenNeuro ds004504 dataset (36 AD, 29 controls). EEG Logistic Regression achieved the strongest mean cross-validated performance (accuracy 0.846, balanced accuracy 0.848, F1 0.849, ROC-AUC 0.948), with feature patterns consistent with AD-related EEG slowing, and was deployed as a public research prototype.

papers.title: MERIT: A No-Code Platform for Unifying High-Precision Cognitive Assessment Across Laboratory and Real-World Settings
papers.summary: This paper quantified how stimulus-timing jitter affects EEG event-related potentials and simulated reaction-time measures, finding that N170 tolerates up to 15.8 ms jitter while MMN and P3 tolerate more than 20 ms, and that jitter tail shape matters. It then introduced MERIT, a no-code platform combining a visual task builder, native mobile apps, and LSL streaming, achieving inter-stimulus-interval SD of 0.71–0.96 ms on current phones/tablets and 3.73 ms on a 2019 budget Android phone, all below the N170 timing ceiling.

papers.title: Prediction of Post-Cardiac Arrest Seizures Using Heart Rate Variability.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
papers.summary: The study developed a heart rate variability-based support vector machine model to predict post-cardiac arrest seizures and identified the optimal prediction window. Performance was highest 15-20 minutes before seizure onset, with an AUC of 0.812 at 18 minutes, and low frequency, sample entropy, high frequency, and LF/HF ratio increased in seizure segments.

papers.title: Brain state-contingent stimulation to probe task-dependent functional networks.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: This review proposes a theoretical and methodological framework for brain state-contingent TMS that uses real-time control of large-scale functional networks, rather than only local oscillatory features, to deliver stimulation when a predefined task-modulated network pattern is expressed. It defines a workflow from offline operationalization to real-time stimulation and aims to improve conditional causal inference, reproducibility, and clinical translation of TMS-EEG.

papers.title: A significant enrichment that is not: spatial nulls, co-expression, and the imaging transcriptomics of EEG alpha-power genetics
papers.summary: This imaging transcriptomics study tested whether alpha-power-associated genes are enriched in cortical alpha generators and found that a field-standard spin test suggested enrichment (continuous p_spin = 0.022), but the signal was not band-specific, did not replicate across alpha phenotypes, and was unremarkable against matched random gene sets (p_geneset = 0.33). No result survived FDR correction across 24 tests (minimum q = 0.127), demonstrating that a spin-significant, surrogate-corroborated enrichment can be fully explained by gene-set co-expression.

papers.title: 20 Hz tACS engages striatal THINs to enhance β-band synchrony and motor drive.
papers.summary: In 18-month-old male mice, 20 Hz tACS over M1 for 7 days under sevoflurane anesthesia was associated with higher post-anesthesia reaching success, increased β-band power, elevated striatal dopamine release, and enhanced striatal THIN activation compared with sham. Optogenetic THIN activation recapitulated motor improvement and β-band enhancement, while THIN inhibition reduced successful attempts and β-band power, implicating striatal dopamine, THINs, and β-band synchrony in post-anesthesia motor recovery.

papers.title: Img2EEG: A Scalable and Interpretable Encoding Framework for Simulating Human EEG Responses to Visual Inputs
papers.summary: Img2EEG is a participant-specific image-to-EEG encoding framework integrating hierarchical visual and semantic representations to generate temporally resolved multichannel EEG responses. Trained on THINGS EEG2 and scaled to 1.28 million ImageNet images to produce over 12 million synthetic EEG responses, it generalized to unseen images, reproduced classic neural responses such as the face-sensitive N170, and supported cross-dataset visual reconstruction.

papers.title: Hybrid EEG-EMG intention decoding for real-time triggering of a lower-limb exoskeleton.
papers.summary: The study developed a hybrid EEG-EMG intention decoding system using a BiLSTM detector for real-time triggering of a lower-limb exoskeleton. The hybrid detector achieved higher classification accuracy (left: 91.3%; right: 86.6%) and shorter mean triggering latency (left: 0.29 s; right: 0.28 s) than EMG-only or EEG-only approaches.

papers.title: The Neuroscience of Marketing: Noninvasive Neuromarketing Methods for Understanding Consumer Choice and Priorities.
papers.summary: This scoping review systematically compiles evidence on non-invasive neuromarketing tools (EEG, fMRI, TMS, Steady State Topography, MEG) for measuring consumer attention, affective arousal, memory encoding, and valuation. It proposes a method selection matrix linking common research and applied questions to suitable measurement strategies, and discusses methodological and ethical challenges.

papers.title: Quantitative Electroencephalography Correlates With Acute Neurologic Events in Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: A Pediatric Case Series.
papers.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
papers.summary: This pediatric case series of two patients on ECMO who underwent continuous EEG monitoring within 6 hours of cannulation analyzed quantitative EEG metrics, including global suppression percentage (SP) and total power (TP). Acute neurologic insults—cardiac arrest, cerebral infarction, and intracranial hemorrhage—were associated with marked increases in global SP and concurrent decreases in TP, highlighting an inverse relationship supporting further investigation of qEEG as a real-time marker of cortical suppression.

papers.title: Stage-specific EEG spectral signatures of primary insomnia: regional and sex-related differences across NREM and REM sleep.
papers.summary: Analyzed EEG spectral power across frontal, central, and occipital regions in 50 primary insomnia patients and 50 healthy sleepers, using explainable machine learning to identify stage-specific biomarkers. NREM-based models outperformed REM-based models; reduced delta power and elevated beta activity in central regions were dominant predictors of insomnia, with sex-related differences in spectral power and feature importance.

papers.title: Voice and linguistic features support early attentional filtering of irrelevant stimuli
papers.summary: In this EEG study, listeners attended to a lateralized stream of target syllables while ignoring distractors, which varied in voice and linguistic content. Both voice and linguistic dissimilarity independently and additively enhanced early target-evoked EEG responses and supported target recall, demonstrating that high-level linguistic features support early attentional filtering of irrelevant stimuli.

papers.title: Theta synchronization coordinates ventral temporal and medial temporal coding of human face familiarity.
papers.summary: Combining single-neuron recordings, intracranial EEG, and multi-scale connectivity analyses in human ventral temporal cortex (VTC) and medial temporal lobe (MTL), the study shows that theta-frequency phase locking of MTL neurons is associated with face familiarity and familiarization, complementing firing-rate signals. Familiarity was linked to enhanced VTC-MTL theta synchronization, especially between VTC visual-feature-coding and MTL familiarity-coding channels, with theta-frequency spike-iEEG coherence suggesting MTL phase locking is coordinated with large-scale VTC activity.

papers.title: Tracing the epistemic arc: Distinct physiological signatures for curiosity, insight, understanding and liking when viewing visual art
papers.summary: Two preregistered experiments used the 'title effect' with visual art to trace an epistemic arc from curiosity to insight (aha), understanding, and liking. Behavioral (N=55) and multimodal (EEG, ECG, eye tracking; N=49) data showed that understanding and curiosity were decodable from physiological signals, aha was decodable from pupil size but not EEG, and a fast initial EEG response linked to aesthetic liking.

papers.title: Functional connectivity theory-based neurophysiological profiles associated with emotional competence and clinical judgment in nursing students: A cluster analysis.
papers.summary: This cluster analysis of 212 nursing students used portable two-channel EEG to identify two neurophysiological profiles based on hemispheric balance and interhemispheric connectivity. Students with an integrated profile showed significantly higher emotional utilization, emotional self-efficacy, and overall clinical judgment, supporting a link between functional brain organization and human-centered competencies.

papers.title: Agomelatine as augmentation therapy with second-generation antipsychotics for negative symptoms of schizophrenia: An open-label randomised clinical trial and electroencephalogram-derived model for treatment response prediction.
papers.summary: In an open-label randomized trial of 74 schizophrenia outpatients with prominent negative symptoms, adding agomelatine 25 mg/day to second-generation antipsychotics reduced PANSS negative symptom factor scores versus antipsychotics alone from Week 8 (EMM difference -1.79) through Week 12 (EMM difference -2.65). Exploratory SVM models using EEG distinguished treatment responders from non-responders with AUC 0.91, implicating left frontotemporal changes.

papers.title: Vagus Nerve Stimulation Exerts Disease-Modifying Effects in Epileptic Rats by Enhancing Hippocampal Adenosine Signalling.
papers.summary: Investigated the disease-modifying mechanisms of vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) in a pilocarpine-induced rat model of temporal lobe epilepsy, focusing on hippocampal adenosine signaling. VNS acutely increased extracellular adenosine, reduced spontaneous seizure frequency and duration, improved spatial memory, suppressed adenosine kinase overexpression, and restored A1 receptor expression; these effects persisted after a 4-week stimulation-free period and were reversed by A1 receptor blockade.

papers.title: Multimodal neuroimaging fusion in presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy: current evidence, clinical integration, and future directions.
papers.summary: This critical narrative review examines how structural MRI, FDG-PET, ictal SPECT/SISCOM, MEG/ESI, fMRI, DTI, and arterial spin labeling are fused through co-registration and machine learning for presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy. It organizes evidence by clinical scenario such as MRI-negative and extratemporal epilepsy and argues that improved localization confidence does not automatically translate to seizure freedom, so multimodal imaging augments rather than replaces multidisciplinary evaluation.

papers.title: Analysis of pediatric absence epilepsy electroencephalograms using a mining-based association rule approach: A cross-sectional study based on realistic data.
papers.summary: Applied association rule mining to clinically labeled EEG data from children with absence epilepsy to identify co-occurrence patterns among discharge morphology, scalp distribution, and seizure duration. Key rules included polyspike-and-wave→spike-and-wave (confidence 1.000) and mesial temporal→central involvement (confidence 0.968), but the small single-center sample limits generalizability, so findings are exploratory.

papers.title: Multimodal Approaches to Visual Experimental Research: Imaging, Electrophysiology, and Behavior.
papers.summary: This review proposes a systematic paradigm for in vivo visual phenotyping of animal models based on three complementary pillars: imaging, electrophysiology, and behavioral testing. It details methodological principles of each approach and advocates for integrative analytical strategies linking macroscopic visual deficiencies to microcircuit dysfunction.

papers.title: Progress of Digital Technologies in the Perioperative Management of Postoperative Delirium Among Older Adults.
papers.summary: This review summarizes advances in digital technologies, including machine learning-based predictive models, wearable sensors, EEG monitoring, and large language models, for identifying postoperative delirium risk and supporting clinical decisions in older adults. It highlights the limitations of traditional risk assessment tools and the potential of these technologies for precision perioperative management.

papers.title: Prevention of postoperative delirium with transcranial alternating current stimulation: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
papers.summary: This two-stage randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial will enroll elderly patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery to identify the optimal frequency-plus-montage and intensity of transcranial alternating current stimulation for preventing postoperative delirium. The primary outcome is incidence of postoperative delirium.

papers.title: Frequency-specific QEEG spectral power correlates of positive and negative symptom severity in recent-onset schizophrenia.
papers.summary: In 18 patients with recent-onset schizophrenia spectrum disorders, resting-state QEEG spectral power was correlated with symptom severity. Higher frontal/central/temporal delta power correlated with positive symptoms, while elevated central-parietal theta and gamma power associated with negative symptoms and general psychopathology.

papers.title: Pediatric stroke in inborn errors of metabolism: clinical characteristics, neuroimaging features, and short-term outcomes.
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study characterized pediatric stroke associated with inborn errors of metabolism in 44 patients. Mitochondrial disorders and homocystinuria were common etiologies; poorer outcomes (mRS 4-6) were associated with generalized epileptiform discharges with diffuse slowing on EEG, while favorable outcomes correlated with focal or normal EEG findings, and outcomes varied by etiology.

papers.title: Subthalamic DBS Engages Right-lateralized Frontal Control to Improve Gait Adaptation in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.summary: Combining kinematics, EEG, and FDG-PET in 12 Parkinson's disease patients, this study characterized gait adaptation during virtual-reality obstacle avoidance under active vs. paused subthalamic deep brain stimulation. Active STN-DBS increased thalamic and right superior frontal gyrus metabolism, and right-lateralized SFG activity correlated with gait adaptation improvement.

papers.title: Event-related potential correlates of ESS-C-defined relapse-risk status in clinically stable patients with schizophrenia: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 60 clinically stable schizophrenia patients stratified by ESS-C relapse-risk status and 30 healthy controls, P3 amplitude was significantly higher in the relapse-risk group than in controls, and ESS-C-defined relapse-risk status was associated with P3 amplitude after adjustment. N2 amplitude positively correlated with negative symptom severity.

papers.title: From brain to heart: a single-centre study of ictal and post-ictal asystole in epilepsy.
papers.summary: A retrospective analysis of 15,578 patients undergoing prolonged video-EEG monitoring identified 8 patients (0.05%) with ictal asystole (IA), predominantly in temporal lobe epilepsy, where 47 of 127 ictal events progressed to asystole and bradycardia preceded 95.7% of asystolic events. The study highlights the clinical features and management of IA and stresses considering IA in epilepsy patients with unexplained syncope or falls.

papers.title: Adolescent development accelerates responses to input in human neocortical neurons
papers.summary: Using patch-clamp electrophysiology and Patch-Seq in neurosurgically resected pediatric human brain slices and age-matched mouse slices, the study found that human Layer 2/3 pyramidal neurons show postnatal changes in physiology aligned with a more directed, feedforward architecture, including faster spike latencies and selective acceleration of early spiking. Linear modeling of Patch-Seq data identified BK-type calcium-activated potassium channels as key drivers of human postnatal changes in spike train dynamics between childhood and adolescence, further tested through pharmacology and computational modeling.

papers.title: Who is to blame? Outcome controllability and error attribution differentially shape cognitive preparation and feedback evaluation.
papers.summary: This EEG study manipulated performance feedback to dissociate self-attributed from system-attributed errors in 35 participants. Manipulated feedback slowed responses via reduced drift rates, attenuated cue-related occipital alpha and sensorimotor beta power decreases, and system-attributed errors elicited stronger midfrontal theta responses than self-attributed errors.

papers.title: Molecularly diverse glycinergic interneurons in the medial deep dorsal horn are interposed between primary sensory afferents and spinal Shox2 interneurons.
papers.summary: Identified glycinergic (GlyT2) interneurons in the medial deep dorsal horn as the inhibitory interneurons interposed between primary sensory afferents and spinal Shox2 interneurons in uninjured mice. Electrophysiology showed afferent stimulation evokes mostly excitatory putative monosynaptic currents in these GlyT2 interneurons, and these cells express multiple deep dorsal horn molecular markers.

papers.title: Efficacy and neural mechanisms of transcranial direct current stimulation for social function in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 RCTs (N=357, ages 4-21) found that transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) significantly improved social functioning in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (SMD = -0.51) and produced significant overall neurofunctional modulations (SMD = 1.03). Neurophysiological effects were largest for fNIRS (SMD = 1.32) and EEG (SMD = 1.16), whereas ERP effects were modest and non-significant (SMD = 0.37); neuro-behavioral consistency was dissociated across levels.

papers.title: Studying dynamic sound source localization in a virtual maze with EEG and psychophysics.
papers.summary: The study used a virtual-reality maze with EEG and psychophysics to investigate dynamic sound source localization during simulated locomotion and real head movements, finding high behavioral accuracy and a robust Mismatch Negativity (MMN) component. The results suggest faithful extraction of source location despite self-motion, compatible with a predictive-coding framework, though the authors note the physical variation was narrower than intended.

papers.title: Case Report: A case of anti-mGluR1 antibody-associated encephalitis treated with efgartigimod combined with rituximab.
papers.summary: A case report of a 16-year-old male with anti-mGluR1 antibody-associated encephalitis who did not respond to first-line corticosteroids but showed significant clinical improvement after sequential therapy with efgartigimod followed by rituximab, with mRS score decreasing from 4 to 3 and SARA score from 40 to 13, and continued improvement at 12-month follow-up. The case suggests a potential synergistic effect of efgartigimod and rituximab in this rare autoimmune disorder.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
